note: Water, sky, cloud and bird modules (water.js, sky.js, atmosphere.js). Every texture these modules use is generated in the browser at start-up by code in water.js / atmosphere.js (tileable value-noise fBm, a detail normal map, a cloud mask, a cloud puff and the baked shore-distance field). No third-party image, model or shader asset is shipped, so this file lists what was consulted rather than what was copied.

consulted.author: three.js authors
consulted.used_for: Reference for how a NodeMaterial takes a custom fragmentNode under WebGPURenderer, and for r170 TSL idioms. Not shipped: WaterMesh is a flat reflector with a scrolling normal map and has no wave displacement, no depth colour and no surf, so water.js is written from scratch.

consulted.author: three.js authors (Preetham model, zz85)
consulted.used_for: Reference for the vertexNode trick that pins a sky dome to the far plane (position.z = position.w), and for varyingProperty usage. The Preetham scattering itself is not used: the key art's sky is a painted gradient, so sky.js is a hand-tuned three-stop gradient.

consulted.licence: project art, not redistributed with the site
consulted.author: Skillstorm
consulted.used_for: Colour reference only. Sea, shelf, foam, haze and sky colours were sampled from it and then inverted through the ACES tone-mapping curve so the rendered result matches the painting.
